=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.

records.raw:
Leading JD gives the best chance of losing this trick. Three diamonds (AD, KD and QD) beat it, and they are spread among the other players. Anyone holding one must follow suit, so the JD will very likely be beaten. If it wins anyway, it only costs 1 point plus whatever else falls.

The clubs are a poor lead because only AC beats my club cards. My aces would almost surely take the trick.

JD

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: the next trick → a new hand is dealt → your hand → the lead → the lead is played → the lead is announced → what each follower may play → the followers play → the followers' cards are played → the reveal → the trick is scored → the sweeper → the winner leads next → the totals → the reversis → after the last trick.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 4, Dirac. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: the next trick → a new hand is dealt → your hand → the lead → the lead is played → the lead is announced → what each follower may play → the followers play → the followers' cards are played → the reveal → the trick is scored → the sweeper → the winner leads next → the totals → the reversis → after the last trick.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: the next trick → a new hand is dealt → your hand → the lead → the lead is played → the lead is announced → what each follower may play → the followers play → the followers' cards are played → the reveal → the trick is scored → the sweeper → the winner leads next → the totals → the reversis → after the last trick.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_lead     answer with one of the options you are given
  the_followers_play answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. === Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 4, Dirac. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: the next trick → a new hand is dealt → your hand → the lead → the lead is played → the lead is announced → what each follower may play → the followers play → the followers' cards are played → the reveal → the trick is scored → the sweeper → the winner leads next → the totals → the reversis → after the last trick.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_lead     answer with one of the options you are given
  the_followers_play answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.

=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: the next trick → a new hand is dealt → your hand → the lead → the lead is played → the lead is announced → what each follower may play → the followers play → the followers' cards are played → the reveal → the trick is scored → the sweeper → the winner leads next → the totals → the reversis → after the last trick.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Quick Reversis ===

Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Quick Reversis is for four players, seats 1 to 4. Every player's total starts at 0; lower is better.

The deck has 24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 9 and 8 in each of Spades (S), Hearts (H), Diamonds (D) and Clubs (C). Within a suit the ranking is A (highest), K, Q, J, 9, 8. There are no trumps. Cards are written like 'QH' (Queen of Hearts).

Card points: each Ace counts 4, each King 3, each Queen 2 and each Jack 1. Nines count 0 and eights 0. The exception is the Jack of Hearts (the Quinola, JH), which counts 5. Each hand contains 44 points in total.

The game has 4 hands of 6 tricks each, 24 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a hand (rounds 1, 7, 13 and 19): the 24 cards are shuffled and 6 are dealt face down to each player. Each player sees only their own hand. The leader of the first trick of hand h is seat h. The sweeper is set to none (0).

Each trick: (1) The leader plays any one card from their hand face up; its suit is the led suit, and it is announced. (2) The other three players each choose one card at the same moment, without seeing each other's choices. A player who holds a card of the led suit must play one (only those cards are offered); a player who holds none may play any card. (3) All cards are revealed together. (4) The highest card of the led suit wins the trick; cards of other suits never win. (5) The points of the 4 cards played are added up and the trick winner adds them to their total. (6) Played cards leave the game for the rest of the hand. (7) The sweeper is updated: on the first trick of a hand, the sweeper becomes the trick winner; on later tricks, if the trick winner is not the sweeper, the sweeper becomes none (0); if the trick winner is the sweeper, the sweeper stays. (8) The trick winner leads the next trick. (9) Every player's total is announced.

End of a hand (after tricks 6, 12, 18 and 24): if the sweeper is a player (that player took all 6 tricks, a reversis), that player subtracts 44 from their total, so the hand counts 0 for them, and each other player adds 15 to their total. If the sweeper is none, no totals are adjusted.

There is no table talk.

After round 24 the game ends. The player with the lowest total wins. If two or more players tie for the lowest total, the game is a draw and they share the result.
